question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Slow to 10 mph and proceed.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.
note: Stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading students while its red lights are flashing and stop arm is extended; don't pass.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:An area designated for road construction workers.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: Crosswalks designate where pedestrians may cross the road and may be marked by white solid lines or may be unmarked at some intersections.

question: If you repeatedly drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and keep passing, what is likely to happen?
options: a:It will help prevent traffic congestion.,b:Your chance of a collision increases.,c:You will reach your destination much faster and more safely.
note: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads — every pass raises the chance of a crash.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:With all four wheels off the traveled portion of the highway.,b:Stop in the right lane.,c:Stop where you are and wait for help.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, move it off the main travel lanes so it does not block traffic or create a hazard.

question: Which statement about backing your vehicle is true?
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing is always hazardous because visibility is limited; use caution and helpers when necessary.

question: In a vehicle equipped with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat when the vehicle has airbags to reduce injury risk.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign is a:
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Warning sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special conditions or hazards ahead; they are usually yellow or orange.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop your vehicle?
options: a:Where there is a red traffic light.,b:Both of the above.,c:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
note: You must come to a complete stop at steady or flashing red lights and obey any police officer directing traffic, regardless of signals.

question: What is true about changing lanes safely?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,b:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.,c:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and look over the appropriate shoulder to verify the adjacent lane is clear of vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles.

question: To be able to turn quickly, your hands should be placed:
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Both hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel to promote comfortable, controlled turns, especially at higher speeds.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must be given the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, where should you start the turn?
options: a:From any lane as long as it is safe.,b:From the center lane.,c:From the lane closest to the left curb.
note: Begin left turns from the far left lane when turning from one one-way street onto another one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it appropriate to always drive slower than the surrounding traffic?
options: a:No — driving significantly slower can block traffic and may be illegal.,b:Yes — it is always safer to drive more slowly than others.,c:Yes — it is a recommended defensive driving technique.
note: You should drive slower in poor conditions but not impede normal traffic flow; blocking traffic can result in a citation.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.,c:Pull off the road
note: If you stop on the highway shoulder, turn on emergency flashers and remain in the vehicle when possible; walking along an interstate is extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to slow down and proceed with caution; no full stop is required unless needed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is prohibited:
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: Never make U-turns on or near curves or hills because you may not see approaching traffic or pedestrians and could cause a collision.

question: Why increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.,b:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,c:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large vehicles block visibility and the drivers may not see you. Increase following distance to see around the vehicle and to give yourself more time to react.

question: What should you do prior to entering a curve?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Activate your turn signal.
note: Slow down before entering a curve; do not brake suddenly while in the curve.

question: Reaction time becomes slower after which activity?
options: a:Working hard.,b:Sleeping.,c:Drinking alcohol.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, impairs vision and alertness, and degrades driving skills.

question: Which statement about driving and medications is true?
options: a:Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.,b:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,c:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving. Many cold and allergy medications cause drowsiness; know how medicines affect you before driving.

question: Why is night driving more challenging?
options: a:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes judging distances and speed of other vehicles difficult; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

question: When passing another car, you should sound your horn if the other car is:
options: a:Signaling a right turn.,b:Driving very slowly in the right lane.,c:About to turn into your lane.
note: Use your horn to warn a driver who is about to turn into your lane and does not see you; use it to help avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane only when:
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:You have cleared the passed vehicle's front bumper.,c:You are at least 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror to ensure enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Go through the intersection without stopping.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: Police officer directions override traffic signals. Follow the officer's instruction to proceed through the intersection.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you set your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,b:Keep the wheels straight.,c:Turn the wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb; when downhill, turn them toward the curb.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean at an intersection?
options: a:The light will soon turn green.,b:The same as a yield sign.,c:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop then proceed when clear.
note: A flashing red requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when safe.

question: What action must you take when approaching an octagonal traffic sign?
options: a:Turn immediately.,b:Stop completely and yield to others with the right-of-way.,c:Slow down.
note: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A prudent driver should:
options: a:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way when it helps prevent a collision.,b:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Do not assume you always have the right-of-way. Yielding when it prevents a crash is a safer choice.

question: Having a driver's license is considered a:
options: a:A requirement.,b:Privilege.,c:A right.
note: Driving is a privilege granted by the state and can be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, which action is safest?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up to get away from them.
note: Avoid confrontation with aggressive drivers; safely yield or change lanes to remove yourself from the situation.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and its stop arm extended, when may motorists proceed?
options: a:As soon as all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted only.,c:Only after the lights are off
note: Motorists must remain stopped until the bus retracts its stop arm, turns off flashing reds, and begins moving.

question: Why should you avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks in their rearview mirrors.,c:Because large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
note: Due to their size and weight, large vehicles take longer to stop; sudden stops in front of them risk collisions.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving dangerous?
options: a:It causes the driver to worry about call costs.,b:It draws other drivers' attention away from the road.,c:It occupies the driver's eyes
note: Cell phone use while driving distracts eyes, hands, and attention, increasing crash risk even for skilled drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, you should begin your turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the centerline.,b:The right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, begin in the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the nearest legal lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked cars than the oncoming vehicles.
note: When faced with oncoming traffic one side and parked cars the other, choose a middle course to maximize clearance from both.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you use to help others see you?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Use low beams as dusk approaches; high beams should only be used where no other vehicles are present.

question: Which statement about braking and accelerating is correct?
options: a:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,b:Use your left foot to brake.,c:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake. Apply brakes smoothly with gradually increasing pressure for a controlled stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in a construction zone, what's the best approach?
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected and proceed with extra caution.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones have unexpected hazards — slow down and be alert to changing conditions and workers.

question: What important action should you take when making a turn?
options: a:Always move to the left lane.,b:Check traffic in all directions.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before turning, look to the rear and both sides of your vehicle and adjust speed as needed to turn safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a designated left-turn lane with oncoming traffic, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels left to be ready to turn.,b:Move to the left of the center lane to prepare.,c:Signal about 100 feet before and keep wheels straight until you actually turn.
note: Start signaling early and keep the wheels pointed straight ahead until you begin the turn to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Follow more closely than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Always remain to the right of the truck and wait to pass.,c:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.
note: Large trucks have greater stopping distances and larger blind spots — keep extra following distance.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction because of standing water, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed to improve traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to regain control.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes.
note: If you begin to hydroplane, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually without braking; braking can make the situation worse.

question: What happens as your BAC increases?
options: a:You become more sober.,b:You become more intoxicated.,c:You become more coordinated.
note: As blood alcohol concentration rises, a person's level of intoxication and impairment increases.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:Increase your speed.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection when it is safe, yielding to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: What is a common effect of excessive speed?
options: a:It often leads to high-risk decision-making.,b:It increases your ability to react to hazards.,c:It does not increase crash risk.
note: Excessive speed contributes to risky choices and is a leading factor in crashes.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the lane adjacent to the solid line.,b:Permitted from the lane adjacent to the broken line.,c:Prohibited from both directions.
note: When a broken yellow is next to a solid yellow, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line only.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic go in the same direction.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing is permitted when it is safe.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line separates lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions; passing is permitted when clear.

question: To help prevent hydroplaning on wet roads you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Slow down.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Reduce speed when the pavement is wet to improve tire contact with the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Exiting a freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.,c:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
note: Slow down to a safe speed before entering a downhill curve; braking in the curve increases risk of skidding.

question: To avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at speeds suitable for ideal conditions.,b:Apply brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to reduce speed in wet conditions.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,b:Both of the above.,c:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see. Be extra cautious near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

question: When should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,c:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
note: When parked on a hill or slope, turn your wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:They have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:They are areas where cars have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are so close they restrict the truck driver's ability to maneuver safely.
note: "No zones" are blind spot areas around large vehicles where passenger cars may disappear from the truck driver's view or be too close for the truck to stop or maneuver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit in residential areas?
options: a:30 mph,b:25 mph,c:20 mph
note: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in residential districts is 25 mph. Be especially alert for children near schools, playgrounds, and neighborhoods.

question: When reversing, what is the correct technique?
options: a:Press hard on the gas pedal to maneuver quickly.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Look through the rear window while backing up.
note: When backing, look directly through the rear window and reverse slowly; mirrors do not show everything behind you.

question: Only which factor can lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to metabolize and lower BAC; nothing else accelerates this process.

question: When conditions require you to drive with headlights on, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or snow; high beams can reflect back and cause glare, and parking lights are insufficient for driving visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to crossing traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a yield sign you must slow down or stop if necessary and give right-of-way to crossing or merging traffic that presents a conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you end up?
options: a:Turn into the first lane of the one-way street.,b:Turn into any lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning, move from the lane nearest your direction into the first legal lane on the one-way street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means you must:
options: a:You are traveling in the wrong direction.,b:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign (come to a complete stop).,c:Not proceed until it changes to green.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop at the stop line or crosswalk; yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may not proceed in the indicated direction until the signal changes.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,c:Drivers may proceed without stopping.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in that direction until the signal changes to green or a green arrow appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what is the most likely result?
options: a:You may interfere with traffic and could receive a citation.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving skills.
note: Driving much slower than traffic can block normal movement and may result in a citation; match traffic speed when safe and legal.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.,b:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,c:So other road users know your intentions.
note: Continuous signaling alerts other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians about your intended movement.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up to pass hazards quickly.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Tires have less traction on wet or icy roads; reduce speed to maintain control.

question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,b:Slow down but never stop.,c:Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign, give way to traffic already in the lanes you intend to enter; stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green traffic light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Follow the vehicle ahead and enter the intersection.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
note: Do not enter an intersection you cannot clear. Blocking intersections is illegal and unsafe even when you have a green light.

question: When must you use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:In fog.,c:On a freeway.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams will reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:Other drivers when they want to slow down.,c:So the truck driver has room to stop and because trucks need longer stopping distances.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances; do not pull in front of a truck and then slow suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, how can you avoid merging traffic entering from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Slow down and stay in the right lane.,b:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,c:Maintain your speed and lane position always.
note: When it is safe, move left to avoid areas where vehicles are merging from on-ramps on the right.

question: How can you make room for vehicles entering the freeway?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Merge into a different lane when possible to create a gap.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: When safe, merge into the next lane to make space for entering traffic; if you cannot, adjust your speed to allow them to merge smoothly.

question: What is true about large trucks compared to passenger vehicles?
options: a:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow very quick stops.,c:They take longer to stop than passenger cars.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances than passenger vehicles; a truck at 55 mph may need almost twice the distance.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you should:
options: a:Expect a traffic light ahead.,b:Not pass.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow centerline indicates that passing is prohibited from your lane.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, drivers approaching from either direction must:
options: a:Stop only if they are traveling in the same direction as the bus.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop only if there are children in the street.,c:Stop regardless of their direction of travel.
note: When a school bus is stopped to load or unload children with flashing red lights and stop arm extended, all approaching vehicles from both directions must stop.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots can be checked using only your rearview mirror.,b:Blind spots are eliminated with one outside mirror.,c:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
note: Even with proper mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks have much larger blind areas than cars.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is true?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the right.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the left.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited for both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on city streets?
options: a:So you can keep up with traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop.,c:To see potential hazards earlier.
note: On freeways, looking further ahead helps detect hazards, merging traffic, and changes in speed earlier.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, you should turn your front wheels:
options: a:Toward the center of the road (left).,b:Toward the side of the road (right).,c:Straight ahead.
note: When parking downhill on a road with or without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you not start across an intersection because you might block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Unless you entered on a green light.,b:Under any circumstances you should avoid entering if you cannot clear it before the light turns red.,c:Unless you entered on a yellow light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it before the light turns red; blocking an intersection can lead to a citation.

question: When is a wet highway surface most likely to be especially slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:If it has been raining several hours.,c:If it has just begun to rain.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery when rain first starts because oil and dirt on the pavement mix with the rain to form a slick film.

question: Even a small amount of alcohol in the blood can affect a driver's what?
options: a:Knowledge.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Any amount of alcohol can impair judgment and coordination, reducing your ability to drive safely.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: If the vehicle skids, release the gas or brake to help regain balance and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: On the highway, consistently scanning far ahead of your vehicle primarily helps to:
options: a:Help you keep up with traffic.,b:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allow you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Looking far ahead lets you anticipate problems and adjust speed or position smoothly, reducing sudden maneuvers and collisions.

question: Roads are especially slippery just after it starts to rain. When the road is slippery, you should:
options: a:Test your tires' traction by accelerating while going uphill.,b:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.,c:Avoid fast turns or sudden stops and drive more slowly.
note: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Slow down and avoid quick steering or braking to reduce the chance of skidding.

question: To stay aware of traffic behind you you should:
options: a:Turn and look out your back window each time.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.
note: Drivers should frequently check the rearview mirror to stay aware of the location and behavior of traffic behind them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but do not see a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,b:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,c:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: If you cannot safely merge, slow on the ramp until a gap appears. Stopping at the end of the ramp leaves you with insufficient room to accelerate and merge.

question: If you're about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Brace yourself by pressing into the seat back.,b:Press your head against the head restraint.,c:Release your seat belt.
note: If hit from behind, do not release your seat belt; brace against the seat and head restraint to reduce injury.

question: Children under age 16 in a moving vehicle must:
options: a:Be restrained at all times.,b:Be restrained only on freeways.,c:Be restrained at the parent's discretion.
note: Delaware law requires that child passengers be properly restrained. Ensure all occupants are using appropriate seat belts or child restraints before driving.

question: After a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage, what should you do if it is safe?
options: a:Not move your vehicle for any reason.,b:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,c:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.
note: If safe, move disabled vehicles out of travel lanes after a crash to reduce hazards and improve traffic flow.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:The railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.,b:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely clear the tracks.,c:You are transporting two or more young children.
note: If you cannot fully clear the tracks, wait until you can to avoid becoming stuck on the rails. Expect a train at any time from either direction.

question: To help avoid skids on slippery surfaces, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Reduce speed before entering curves and intersections; braking on a curve can cause you to skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about roadwork (work) zones?
options: a:Slow only if you think workers are present.,b:Fines are always the same as normal conditions.,c:You must slow down for the Cone Zone.
note: Drivers should slow for Cone Zones and drive carefully; work zone fines are often increased to encourage safe driving.

question: As you near the crest of a hill, you should:
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Keep a steady speed.,c:Be prepared to stop if necessary.
note: You can't see what is just over a hill; reduce speed enough to stop if needed for hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Rely only on the left side mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check the blind spot.,c:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.
note: Glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes. You may need to check several times and also monitor traffic ahead and beside you.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:An antihistamine.,b:A depressant.,c:A stimulant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment and slows reflexes.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline indicates you may cross the line to pass another vehicle on the left when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Only begin to prepare to slow down.
note: If there is imminent danger, sound a sharp blast of the horn to warn the child and others. Use other evasive actions as needed to avoid a crash.

question: If a vehicle has airbags, what is still required for safety?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags supplement seat belts; occupants must still wear lap and shoulder belts for full protection.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to reduce collision risk?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Night driving lowers visibility; increase following distance and use appropriate beam settings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a lane sign showing an arrow with the word "ONLY" beneath it, you should:
options: a:Look for a destination sign to follow instead of the arrow.,b:Always change lanes when you see it.,c:Travel only in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and "ONLY" indicates drivers in that lane must proceed in the direction shown by the arrow.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean for a left turn?
options: a:You should speed up to make the turn before it changes.,b:You don't need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c:Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic — the protected turn is ending.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is sliding left in a skid, what should you do?
options: a:Not turn the wheel.,b:Turn the steering wheel left (in direction of skid).,c:Turn the wheel right (away from skid).
note: When skidding (rear slides left), steer into the skid (left) while easing off accelerator and staying off the brakes, unless ABS requires different braking.

question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:Only if you are stopped and cited.,c:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
note: You are required to have evidence of financial responsibility (proof of insurance) with you when driving and must show it to an officer after a stop or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only after confirming the passed vehicle is fully visible in your inside rearview mirror.

question: Broken yellow lines on the roadway are used to:
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate traffic moving in opposite directions
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposite-direction traffic and indicate passing is permitted when safe.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what is the safest course of action before driving?
options: a:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.
note: Strong emotions impair driving ability. Take time to calm down before getting behind the wheel so you can focus on driving safely.

question: While in a motor vehicle on a highway, it is:
options: a:Legal to drink alcohol while driving if you are not intoxicated.,b:Legal to drink alcohol if you are not the driver.,c:Illegal to drink or possess open containers of alcohol.
note: It is illegal for occupants to possess open containers of alcohol in a motor vehicle while it is being operated. Operating while impaired is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
options: a:Only during the day.,b:Only under ideal driving conditions.,c:Only during the night.
note: The posted maximum is the fastest legal speed under ideal conditions; drive at a safe speed appropriate for conditions.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver.,c:Only if the pedestrians are not using a phone.
note: Drivers must stop at crosswalks to yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Only signal and assume it's safe.,b:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors.,c:Check mirrors and blind spots
note: Always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving laterally.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: Work zones often have workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes; be alert and reduce speed.

question: When may you cross double yellow centerlines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:The yellow line next to the opposite side is broken.,b:The yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:The vehicle in front of you moves right to let you pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means that you may pass when it is safe to do so; a solid line on your side means you may not pass.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the road even if there is no marked crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a full stop
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, then go when it is safe.

question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Allow a larger following distance.,b:Drive more slowly.,c:Be ready to use your horn.
note: Allow at least a three- to four-second following distance behind motorcycles; they can stop quickly and are more vulnerable.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt system, how should you use it?
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: If your vehicle is equipped with both lap and shoulder belts, always wear both for proper protection.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if traffic signals favor the pedestrian.,b:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,c:At all times to avoid striking them
note: Do everything possible to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if they are in the wrong; safety is paramount.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat an intersection where the traffic signal is not operating?
options: a:Drive quickly through to get out of the way of other vehicles.,b:If the intersection is clear,c:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
note: Treat a non-functioning signal as an all-way stop: stop and yield before proceeding unless directed otherwise by police.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may safely return to your lane after passing another vehicle when:
options: a:You have cleared the other vehicle's front bumper.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are about three seconds ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only move back into the original lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring you have enough space.

question: If there is a deep puddle ahead, you should:
options: a:Shift into neutral while driving through it.,b:Avoid it if possible.,c:Maintain the posted speed to make it through.
note: Avoid deep puddles when you can; driving through deep water can cause loss of control or damage to your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do before moving over?
options: a:Slow down abruptly.,b:Only check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify there are no vehicles in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the posted speed limit in Delaware school zones?
options: a:20 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: In Delaware, the speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive with extra caution near schools and playgrounds.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:All pedestrians and drivers to respect your right-of-way.,b:Driving closely to parked cars to allow more room for moving traffic.,c:A person or vehicle unexpectedly entering your lane.
note: Be prepared for pedestrians or drivers suddenly entering the roadway from between parked vehicles; leave space and slow.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the bus moves.
note: You must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children with lights flashing and the stop arm extended, until it resumes motion.

question: What is an effect of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:It reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.,b:It can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,c:It cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Tailgating encourages aggressive responses and increases crash risk; it can also lead to legal penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian starts crossing during a 'Don't Walk' flash and is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
note: Even with a green light, yield to pedestrians already in the intersection until they finish crossing.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Open a window.
note: If you grow tired while driving, stop in a safe place to rest or change drivers; temporary measures are not substitutes for sleep.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, at what minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) does driving become illegal?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older, operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal and dangerous.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, which way should you steer?
options: a:Steer to the left to correct the skid.,b:Steer to the right.,c:Tap brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go (toward the skid) to regain alignment and control.

question: Which substances can impair driving ability?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving; always check medication effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, how do you merge safely?
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for the first two vehicles to pass then drive into the lane.
note: Merge only when there is enough space to accelerate to the flow of traffic safely.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Always use high beams.,b:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,c:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Lower your headlights to low beam when following another vehicle to avoid blinding the driver ahead.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights, you must yield right-of-way by:
options: a:Moving into the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.,b:Driving as close as possible to the right edge of the road and stopping.,c:Stopping immediately even if you are in an intersection.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping; avoid stopping in an intersection. Proceed once the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: At a school crossing sign (pentagon-shaped), what should drivers do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop even without a stop sign.
note: Pentagonal signs indicate school zones or crossings; be alert and prepared to stop for children.

question: A red octagon-shaped sign always means:
options: a:Stop.,b:Do not enter.,c:One-way.
note: An octagonal sign always indicates "STOP." You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

question: Defensive drivers:
options: a:Assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:Expect no breaks and give none.,c:Consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating potential errors by others and being prepared to compensate to reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you not do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and return to your desired exit.,b:Continue on the freeway and find another route.,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder; continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.

question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Use the inside rearview mirror.,b:Use only your side mirror.,c:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
note: Even with mirrors, some blind spots remain; look over your shoulder to verify the area is clear before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: Do not change lanes within an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:You can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds after completing the pass.,c:You can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: You may move back into the right lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating a safe margin.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout, how should you use the brakes?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Use the brakes lightly.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: If a tire suddenly goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down gradually by easing off the gas, and use the brakes lightly.

question: A driver should keep watch:
options: a:Directly in front of the car at all times.,b:Only at the middle of the road.,c:Beside
note: To be a safe driver you must be aware of what is happening all around your vehicle — to the sides, ahead, and behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle moving in the same direction, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:You can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:About three seconds after passing.
note: Do not return to your lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror; always check blind spots first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle?
options: a:Speed up to clear the lane.,b:Pull as far to the right as possible and stop.,c:Move into the right lane and continue slowly until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.

question: What effect does drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you to be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness impairs reaction time, awareness, and judgment much like alcohol or drugs.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what lights should you turn on?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: When you cannot see other vehicles because of dust, smoke, or similar conditions, turn on your headlights so others can see you.

question: Regulatory road signs typically have what background color?
options: a:Green.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs are most often white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green letters or symbols indicating laws.

question: During rainy weather, when are turns or stops most hazardous?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:One half hour after the rain stops.,c:After it has been raining all day.
note: The pavement is most slippery during the first 30 minutes of rain due to accumulated oil and debris mixing with water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady yellow light at an intersection, if you have not entered, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce speed and continue through the intersection regardless.,c:Stop safely if you can.
note: A steady yellow warns the light is changing; if you can stop safely, do so rather than enter on red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:At the posted speed regardless of traffic flow.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of the traffic flow to merge safely without disrupting other drivers.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you do?
options: a:Keep front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb but not use the parking brake.,b:Use the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park; position wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.,c:Have a rear wheel touch the curb.
note: On hills always set the parking brake and place the vehicle in park (or leave in gear); turn wheels so a runaway rolls away from traffic.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads, what is the best action?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: Lower speed on wet roads to reduce hydroplaning risk; do not make sudden steering or braking inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Slow down to let the other driver safely return to the driving lane.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: If you are being passed in a no passing zone, slow down and allow the passing vehicle to return to the lane as safely as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate where there is no acceleration lane, you should:
options: a:Use the shoulder to gain speed before merging.,b:Only enter the interstate after identifying a gap in traffic and then speed to match flow.,c:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up regardless of gaps.
note: If there is no acceleration lane, wait for a safe gap before entering and then accelerate to match traffic speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your driving lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed signals for you to return.,c:When you have signaled for three seconds.
note: Only return to the driving lane when you can see the passed vehicle entirely in your mirror to ensure safe distance.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting choice is best?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Low beams reduce glare and improve visibility in fog; high beams reflect back and worsen visibility.

question: Why should you keep the inside of your windows clean if someone has been smoking?
options: a:Dust tends to settle on the insides of car windows.,b:Smoking causes a film to build up on the glass inside the vehicle.,c:The stale smell can be distracting.
note: Smoke deposits produce a film on glass that reduces visibility; keep windows clean for safety.

question: If your tires feel like they're losing contact with the road surface, what should you do first?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,c:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.
note: If tires lose contact, lift off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until traction returns.

question: What is the effect of slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events?
options: a:Prevents rear-end collisions.,b:Causes traffic congestion.,c:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.
note: Slowing to look at crashes or unusual events (''rubbernecking'') often causes additional congestion and can lead to secondary crashes.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for appointments.,c:Falling asleep and crashing.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time and can lead to falling asleep at the wheel, causing serious crashes.

question: You are driving defensively when you:
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,c:Look only at the car directly in front of you.
note: Defensive driving involves scanning the road, mirrors, and surroundings to anticipate and react to potential hazards.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead at the lights.
note: Look to the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams and maintain lane position.

question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross before you make a right turn. What should you do?
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,b:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,c:Wait until the person crosses the street.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must be given the right-of-way; wait until they have crossed safely before making your turn.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means you may cross to pass another vehicle on the left if it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley or driveway across a sidewalk to enter traffic, you should:
options: a:Expect pedestrians to yield to you.,b:Only stop if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.
note: You must stop before entering or crossing a sidewalk area when coming from an alley or driveway and yield to pedestrians.

question: When should you allow extra following distance for the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When following a passenger vehicle.,b:When following a station wagon.,c:When following a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see; allow extra space to react safely.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?
options: a:Driving in both directions may pass.,b:Next to the broken line may pass.,c:Next to the solid line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your driving lane indicates you may pass when it is safe; a solid line on your side means you may not pass.

question: Which factor affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed into a person's system?
options: a:Intelligence,b:Height,c:Weight
note: Factors affecting alcohol absorption include weight, sex, amount of food in the stomach, and the number of drinks consumed. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Construction zone signs are normally what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange background and black symbols.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols and warn of road work ahead.

question: On a green traffic arrow, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Only yield to pedestrians in the intersection.,b:Yield to any vehicles,c:Wait four seconds before starting the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you the right to turn but you must yield to any remaining vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always travel at what speed?
options: a:At the posted speed limit no matter what.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you even if above limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: Drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions and never exceed the legal limit.

question: When stopped at a railroad with double tracks, when may you proceed?
options: a:As soon as one train has passed.,b:Only when the train is out of sight.,c:Only when you are sure no trains are approaching on either track and the passing train is well clear.
note: At multiple tracks, wait until passing trains are well down the track; another train may be approaching on a second track.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing outside a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop for them.,b:Should honk your horn at them.,c:Do not have to stop for them.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if they are crossing where they should not; stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: When the center of the roadway has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line, and the broken line is next to your lane, it means:
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You may only make right turns here.,c:You are in a passing zone and may pass on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
note: When the broken yellow line is adjacent to your lane, passing from your direction is permitted when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: Why should you not use high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,b:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes.
note: High beams reflect off fog or mist and can reduce your visibility by shining back into your eyes; use low beams instead.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Slow down whenever you see one in the distance.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle to give it space.,c:Make constant visual checks for them.
note: Motorcycles can be hidden in blind spots or missed in quick glances. Drivers should be constantly aware and check for them frequently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is required when turning left at an intersection?
options: a:You should yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before making a left turn; proceed only when safe.

question: Which action helps you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the driver ahead.,b:Relax and focus on driving.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit.
note: Prevent aggression by concentrating on driving, allowing realistic travel time, obeying speed limits, and being forgiving.

question: What do "No passing zone" signs indicate?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:To maintain a steady speed.,c:That it is not safe to pass.
note: A "No passing zone" sign indicates that passing is not permitted and would be unsafe in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Cross the centerline in an intersection.
note: Never change lanes by crossing the centerline while inside an intersection. Always check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

question: What best describes distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: Distracted driving involves activities that take your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving and is a leading factor in collisions.

question: Roads are most slippery at which moment during rainfall?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Road surfaces are especially slippery just after rain begins when oil and residues mix with water.

question: Driving under the influence of medication that impairs your driving is:
options: a:Allowed if your physician prescribes it.,b:Under no circumstances permitted.,c:Allowed if you do not feel drowsy.
note: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance that affects your ability to operate a vehicle safely, including medications.

question: After a train passes and you have stopped at a railroad crossing, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Drive around the lowered gates if it seems safe.,b:Proceed immediately since the first train has passed.,c:Wait for signals to stop flashing and look for a second train.
note: Do not cross until all lights stop flashing, gates are fully raised, and you've checked for additional trains on other tracks.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as a vehicle's speed increases?
options: a:They increase.,b:They decrease.,c:They stay the same.
note: Higher speeds raise stopping distance and the potential impact and severity of a collision — increase following distance as speed rises.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake lightly to slow, then pull off safely.,b:Apply the brake and hold it down hard.,c:Pull over immediately without slowing gradually.
note: If a tire blows, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, brake lightly, and steer to a safe place off the roadway.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver simply makes a mistake.,b:Whenever another vehicle is in your way.,c:When it may help prevent a collision.
note: Use your horn only to avoid collisions; avoid honking to pressure slower drivers or bicyclists.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a driver who cannot see their vehicle's rear (like trucks),c:When following a small passenger car.
note: Large vehicles may have limited rear visibility; increase following distance so they can see you and to see around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed?
options: a:When driving down long,b:When driving in long,c:When driving up long or steep hills.
note: Large trucks typically slow when climbing long or steep grades because they take longer to accelerate.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you get into the car.,b:Before you start driving.,c:Whenever you need to use them while driving.
note: Adjust mirrors (and seat and safety belt) before moving the vehicle; do not do mirror adjustments while driving.

question: How should you drive on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement,b:Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Loose gravel and dirt reduce traction; slow down and allow more distance to stop and to maneuver safely.

question: What can you do to reduce road rage incidents while driving?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Always signal your intentions when changing lanes.
note: Signaling intentions early and obeying traffic laws helps reduce frustration and road rage incidents.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you leaving little space, what should you do first?
options: a:Swerve into the adjacent lane.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal to create space.,c:Honk and step on the brake firmly.
note: Remove pressure from the accelerator to increase the gap without sudden braking or swerving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, check the traffic, and go when it is safe to do so.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection without stopping.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: When roads are snowy or icy, how should you make speed and direction changes?
options: a:It is safe to use your cruise control.,b:Drive as you would under normal conditions.,c:Make changes more gradually than usual.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual steering and speed changes; never use cruise control on these surfaces.

question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield and passenger window.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield.
note: You must be able to see through all of your vehicle's windows and mirrors; remove all snow, ice, and frost before driving.

question: In traffic moving 50–55 mph, you are least likely to be involved in a crash if you:
options: a:Stay within that speed range.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.,c:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
note: Matching the flow of traffic (while obeying speed limits) minimizes speed differentials between vehicles, reducing the chance of collisions.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct action?
options: a:Turn sharply back onto the roadway immediately.,b:Stop where you are.,c:Reduce speed
note: Don't turn back onto the pavement abruptly; slow, check traffic, and re-enter gradually when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you do on the acceleration lane?
options: a:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,b:Check for cars,c:Stop
note: Use the acceleration lane to match highway speeds and merge smoothly into flowing traffic.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken line next to a solid line means traffic next to the broken line may pass when safe, while traffic next to the solid line may not.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, you should:
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive faster to get off the road quickly.
note: When visibility is poor, increase following distance to allow more time to react to hazards you may see late.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take some caffeine pills.,b:Take a break.,c:Try to fight it.
note: If you become tired while driving, stop at the first safe location to rest, nap, or change drivers. Caffeine is not a substitute for rest.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow indicates caution — slow down and be alert for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what should you expect?
options: a:They must always wait off the roadway.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may use the left lane to make the turn.
note: Bicyclists often use the left lane to complete left turns; expect them to behave like vehicles in such cases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, after setting the parking brake you should:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep your wheels facing straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: On an uphill slope with no curb, point the front wheels toward the road edge (to the right) so the vehicle will roll off the roadway rather than into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: What does a pentagon-shaped sign normally indicate?
options: a:School zone or school crossing.,b:Stop sign.,c:Regulatory sign.
note: A five-sided sign indicates a school zone/crossing and warns of children in the area.

question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem while driving, you should:
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane.,b:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road as soon as safe.
note: Get your vehicle away from traffic if possible and turn on emergency flashers so others can see you have trouble.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,c:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if no crosswalk is present; stop and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Use rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
note: Use mirrors and physically look over your shoulder to check blind spots before merging onto a freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always do what?
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Stop,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: Whenever people may cross or enter your path, look left and right to ensure no one is coming into your path of travel.

question: If the vehicle in front of you stops at a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.,c:Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed before proceeding.
note: Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in heavy rain?
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Immediately move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to reduce the chance your tires will ride on a film of water (hydroplaning).

question: A double solid yellow centerline means:
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from your direction of travel.
note: A double yellow centerline prohibits crossing the lines to pass vehicles traveling in either direction.

question: What color and lettering do temporary work zone signs use?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Red background with green writing.
note: Temporary construction and maintenance signs use orange backgrounds with black writing and/or symbols to warn drivers of work zones.

question: Sudden gusts of wind on highways:
options: a:Only cause visibility problems.,b:Only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:Can cause problems for all vehicles.
note: Strong winds can affect vehicles of all sizes and may lower visibility by blowing dust or debris onto the roadway.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in adverse weather like rain or fog. High beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,b:You never need to yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians.,c:You should yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians in the roadway.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking if possible.,c:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, take your foot off the accelerator, and allow the vehicle to slow before braking gently only if necessary. Pull off the road when safe.

question: When driving on a slippery surface like snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.,b:Maintain traction by following other vehicles closely.,c:Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
note: On slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before descending steep hills and increase following distance; pump brakes only if you don't have antilock brakes.

question: Why should you use antifreeze washer fluid in cold climates?
options: a:Cold fluid can scratch your windshield.,b:It will keep the washer fluid from freezing.,c:Moisture can cause cold wiper blades to crack.
note: Antifreeze washer fluid prevents freezing so you can clear salt, dirt, and slush from the windshield in winter.

question: How should you drive under low-visibility conditions due to fog?
options: a:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn on your high beam headlights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights; if visibility is severely limited, pull off the road safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter drugs can greatly impair driving ability and may make you unfit to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:No one.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:Oncoming cars.
note: A vehicle turning left must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight through the intersection.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead with flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Come to a complete stop only until all the children have left the bus.,c:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm is retracted.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have big blind spots; avoid staying alongside them for long and pass safely.

question: What do rumble strips do?
options: a:Through vibration and sound,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
note: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.
