question: If you see pedestrians near the road, how should you proceed?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, what should you assume about the other driver?
options: a:Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.,b:Do not assume they will make room for you to return to your lane.,c:Assume they will maintain a constant speed.
note: Even with signals, do not assume other drivers will create space; verify it is safe before passing.

question: Before moving back into your original lane after passing, what should you see?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Beep your horn.,c:Both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Only return to your lane after passing when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, showing a safe gap.

question: Which vehicle type is required to stop at all railroad crossings?
options: a:A school bus.,b:A dairy truck.,c:A cattle truck.
note: School buses, transit buses, and vehicles carrying hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Brake lightly to slow the vehicle immediately.,b:Brake abruptly to stop the slide.,c:Stay off the brakes and steer in the direction you want the front to go.
note: If you skid, avoid braking; steer gently in the direction you want the vehicle to go until you regain traction.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Drive to the right edge and slow down but stay moving.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping until they have passed; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and wait to drift to a stop.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
note: For vehicles with ABS, press the brake firmly and the system will pump the brakes automatically.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, what should you avoid doing immediately?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Tap or pump the brakes.,c:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
note: When a tire blows out, take your foot off the accelerator, slow down gradually, and do not apply the brakes hard until the vehicle has slowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are approaching an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Proceed through without caution.,b:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,c:Speed up to beat the light.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. Stop if you can safely; otherwise, proceed with caution.

question: How can you help the driver behind you maintain a safe distance?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: Holding a steady speed and signaling early helps following drivers maintain safe spacing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b:Inconvenience drivers.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.
note: Barriers and signs are placed to guide traffic and protect workers by keeping vehicles out of hazardous zones.

question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:As your speed increases,c:You as your speed increases
note: Higher speeds increase the chance of a fatality and require greater following distances. Increase following distance as your speed increases.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're being passed repeatedly while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right when safe.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, use the right lanes unless passing or turning left; move right if you are slower than traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving more slowly than the surrounding traffic is:
options: a:A good idea in all situations.,b:Appropriate if you do not know the speed limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may try to pass unsafely.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can create hazardous passing situations and increase the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
note: Signal both when pulling toward the curb to park and when pulling away to re-enter traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally block an intersection:
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,c:During rush hour traffic.
note: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely; blocking intersections is prohibited.

question: Which behavior may identify someone as an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:The number of passengers in their car.,c:Tendency to drive slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often make sudden, unsafe lane changes and other risky maneuvers; avoid engaging them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already in an intersection and the light changes from green to steady yellow, you should:
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Speed up to get through more quickly.
note: If you are in an intersection when the light turns yellow, clear the intersection as quickly and safely as possible; do not speed up recklessly.

question: In very foggy conditions, you should slow down and:
options: a:Use high beam headlights.,b:Use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers only.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect back and worsen visibility. Fog lights can supplement low beams if equipped.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Slow down and proceed carefully near animals; they may move unpredictably and travel in groups.

question: If your car starts to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: In a skid, do not brake; steer gently in the desired direction until control returns.

question: What does the term BAC refer to?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in a person's blood and is used to assess impairment.

question: If you must park somewhere not usually used for parking, what must you ensure?
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: When parking in an unusual spot, position your vehicle so it doesn't become a hazard and is visible to others.

question: In bad or inclement weather you should:
options: a:Drive in a low gear only.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Steer and brake smoothly.
note: In poor weather, avoid sharp steering and hard braking; make all inputs smooth to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time from your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the right has the right-of-way when vehicles arrive simultaneously; proceed in arrival order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left.,b:The driver who arrived before you.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: Proceed in the order of arrival; the vehicle that arrives first has the right-of-way at a multiway stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Use only the outside mirrors.,c:Look over your shoulder.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors; glance over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams and impairs your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Look straight ahead in your lane.,c:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, avoid looking directly at the lights. Look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to monitor the oncoming vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and the driver on your left arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,c:You have the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. If the other vehicle is on your left, you are to its right and may go first.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian while an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,b:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.,c:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
note: Handle one hazard at a time: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass, then pass the pedestrian if safe to do so.

question: If your car's suspension is worn, what problem can it cause?
options: a:Vehicle control problems and difficulty handling.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: A bad suspension affects ride comfort and vehicle control, making handling unsafe.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow, what helps others see you?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn up instrument panel lights.,c:Turn on only your parking lights.
note: Use your headlights (low beams) when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see you.

question: A school bus is stopped ahead with red lights flashing in your lane. What must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped while the red lights are flashing.,b:Stop and proceed when you think children have exited.,c:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.
note: Stop for a school bus with flashing red lights unless on the opposite side of a divided highway.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, then affects coordination and vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane should you be in before making a left turn from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the left curb.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, start the turn from the lane nearest the left curb and enter the nearest available lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped at a red light that also displays a green arrow for your lane, you may proceed in the arrow's direction if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,c:You wait until the main light changes to green.
note: A green arrow allows you to proceed in the arrow's direction if you are in the correct lane and the way is clear; yield to pedestrians and traffic already in the intersection.

question: Which headlights should drivers use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, or snow. High beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: When in a work zone, how should you manage your following distance?
options: a:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Follow the driver in front of you closely.
note: Maintain a safe distance in work zones to allow time to react to slowed or stopped traffic and to protect workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you judge before starting to pass?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:The distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Always ensure there is sufficient distance and time to pass safely without encountering oncoming traffic.

question: When visibility is reduced by fog, rain, or snow, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Low beam headlights are recommended in fog, rain, or snow because high beams can cause glare and reduce visibility.

question: If the road ahead is flooded, what should you do?
options: a:Not drive through the flooded area; turn around and seek another route.,b:Slam on the brakes.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never attempt to drive through floodwater — it may hide hazards and can sweep your vehicle away. Find an alternate route.

question: When driving at night, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Always use your high beams.
note: At night, increase your following distance when visibility is reduced and avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights to prevent glare.

question: If you park uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the side of the road (right).,c:Toward the center of the road (left).
note: On roads without a curb, turn wheels so the vehicle would roll away from traffic (toward the road edge).

question: Which is a dangerous habit in work zones?
options: a:Only tailgating.,b:Only failing to watch for workers and equipment.,c:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers and equipment.
note: In work zones, do not follow too closely and pay careful attention to workers and equipment; both behaviors are hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians and oncoming vehicles that have the right-of-way.,b:All approaching vehicles regardless of direction.,c:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a Walk signal only.
note: When making a left turn, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians who have the right-of-way.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you anticipate?
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them.,b:That the child may act unpredictably — expect the unexpected.,c:Assume the child is in full control of the bicycle.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; be ready to react and give them plenty of space.

question: When a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is crossing, what must you do?
options: a:Yield only at corners.,b:Tell them where to cross.,c:Yield the right-of-way at all times.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must always be given the right-of-way.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,c:Only when a crossing guard is present.
note: Pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: What is the only proven method to remove alcohol or drug combinations from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Breathe fresh air.,c:Give your body time.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol or impairing drugs; other measures do not lower BAC.

question: If you become tired while driving you should:
options: a:Open a window for fresh air and continue driving.,b:Stop and either rest or change drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue driving.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, stop and get rest or change drivers. Short breaks every hour on long trips help prevent drowsiness.

question: From top to bottom, what is the standard vertical order of traffic lights?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:You red
note: Standard vertical traffic signal order is red at the top, then yellow, then green at the bottom.

question: What do double solid yellow centerline markings indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing for both directions.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be more alert, and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: Which habit blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene (rubbernecking).,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Rubbernecking slows traffic and can create secondary collisions; keep moving and avoid staring at incidents.

question: If an accident causes over $500 in damage, when must you report it?
options: a:Immediately, regardless of who caused it.,b:Only if you were at fault.,c:Only if you are uninsured.
note: Any accident on a public highway that results in $500 or more in property damage must be reported by the driver involved, regardless of fault.

question: When you encounter a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, what must you do?
options: a:Honk your horn as you proceed.,b:Carefully drive around them.,c:Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way; stop and wait until they are safely clear of your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you obey the instructions of a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:Unless you do not see any children present.,c:At all times.
note: Always obey directions from school crossing guards; they supervise pedestrian safety near schools.

question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic if possible.,b:Always maintain your position regardless of circumstances.,c:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.
note: When safe and practical, adjust your position or speed to allow vehicles to merge smoothly into your lane.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in the mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of a vehicle that cannot be seen by using mirrors alone; check them by looking over your shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you permitted to pass another vehicle on the road?
options: a:When a solid line is next to your lane.,b:On a hill or curve.,c:When a broken center line is next to your lane.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane means passing is allowed if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,b:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.,c:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what should you do regarding safety belts?
options: a:Buckle only if you are driving on the highway.,b:Check passengers' belts after starting the car.,c:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers have buckled theirs.
note: Make a habit of fastening your belt and confirming others have buckled before starting the engine.

question: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:0.08 percent or more.,c:Any amount.
note: Delaware enforces zero tolerance for drivers under 21: detection of any alcohol can lead to penalties including license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to turn left on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Whenever you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,c:When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits it.
note: Left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a complete stop and when no sign forbids it.

question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: Do not change lanes suddenly; always signal, check mirrors, and verify blind spots before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making a left turn must yield to:
options: a:No specific vehicles.,b:Passing cars only.,c:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to all oncoming traffic, including bicycles and motorcycles going straight or turning right.

question: How should you change lanes from one lane to another?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:Gradually and carefully.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: Change lanes gradually and carefully only when necessary; every lane change increases the chance of a collision.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than daytime driving?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare mean you cannot see as far at night as during the day. Use headlights and exercise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red signal, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and enter with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop, after which you may proceed when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: What does a pennant-shaped yellow sign indicate?
options: a:Right turns permitted.,b:Right turns only.,c:No passing zone.
note: Pennant-shaped (sideways triangular) yellow signs are used to warn drivers of no passing zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and you have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,b:Come to a safe stop.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon turn red; prepare to stop unless already in the intersection.

question: If you are involved in an accident that causes injury, when must you report it?
options: a:Immediately.,b:Within 24 hours.,c:Within one week.
note: If any person is injured or killed in a traffic accident, notify the police immediately. Leaving the scene before providing required information is a crime.

question: A distraction while driving is:
options: a:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: A driving distraction is anything that diverts your attention from the task of driving. Such distractions can lead to collisions, injuries, and deaths.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge of the road.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly
note: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas to slow naturally, and steer to a safe area before braking lightly when safe.

question: An orange and red triangular sign displayed on the back of a vehicle means:
options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Slow-moving vehicle.
note: Slow-moving vehicles such as farm equipment and some maintenance vehicles display an orange and red triangle to warn other road users.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only to check for vehicles in blind spots.,b:Only when slowing down.,c:Often to monitor how traffic is moving behind you.
note: Frequently check your mirrors so you know the positions and actions of vehicles around you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while the traffic light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,c:Obey the police officer.
note: Drivers must follow instructions from police officers directing traffic, even if they conflict with signs or signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle:
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder. Passing on the shoulder is dangerous because other drivers do not expect you there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light that shows a green arrow, you may proceed in the arrow's direction when:
options: a:You must first come to a complete stop.,b:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,c:You must wait until the light changes.
note: If you are in the lane controlled by a green arrow you may go in the arrow's direction when the way is clear. This applies whether the arrow is shown alone or with other signals.

question: When a vehicle with bright headlights approaches at night, where should you look?
options: a:Look directly at the headlights.,b:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Stop in your lane until the vehicle passes.
note: Avoid looking at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right edge of your lane to avoid being blinded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to block the pass.,b:Brake hard to prevent the pass.,c:Maintain a steady speed and allow the passing vehicle to complete the maneuver.
note: When being passed, maintain constant speed or slow slightly and allow the other vehicle to pass safely and merge back.

question: Your car may begin to hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:35 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds around 35 mph when there is standing water; as speed increases, tires can lose contact with the road.

question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Pass the work zone carefully and avoid slowing down to stare at the scene.,b:Stop to watch the workers.,c:Reduce your following distance.
note: Do not "rubberneck" or slow down to look at unusual events in a work zone. Proceed carefully and maintain a safe following distance.

question: Where are truck blind spots located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the truck.,b:Directly behind the body only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on both sides and directly behind; if you can't see the driver in their mirror, they likely can't see you.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,c:Wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you turn.
note: Do not try to pass between a turning truck or bus and the curb; wait until the larger vehicle completes its turn.

question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas, food, or hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information only.
note: Blue signs are service signs that inform drivers about motorist services like rest areas, food, lodging, and hospitals.

question: When finishing a passing maneuver, how can you tell you have enough room to return to your lane?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
note: Before moving back into the driving lane after passing, be sure there is a safe gap between vehicles. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the driving lane.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard continuous braking on icy or snowy surfaces may lock wheels and lead to loss of steering. Slow down and brake gently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should yield your legal right-of-way:
options: a:Never,b:Often,c:Whenever it helps prevent a collision.
note: Yield your right-of-way when doing so helps prevent a crash. Do not assume other drivers will obey the rules.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights reduce glare from fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How should drivers check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Only the left outside mirror.,c:Look over the left or right shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show all areas around your vehicle; look over the appropriate shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

question: You should increase the following distance between your vehicle and the one ahead when you are:
options: a:Driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,b:Following a small passenger vehicle.,c:Being tailgated by another driver.
note: If another driver is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking; slow gradually or change lanes if safe.

question: Which statement correctly describes having a driver's license?
options: a:It is a legal requirement that cannot be revoked.,b:It is a privilege,c:It is a right
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted under law and can be suspended or revoked for violations.

question: If you damage a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name
note: If you hit parked property, leave a note securely attached with your contact information and report the incident as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking mirrors you should:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder into the lane you want to enter.,b:Never look over your right shoulder.,c:Always slow down in your lane.
note: Always look over your shoulder to check blind spots prior to changing lanes, in addition to mirror checks and signaling.

question: What is the only truly effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Wait — time.,b:Drink strong coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing speeds up the process.

question: On a slippery road, how should your following distance compare to normal?
options: a:Increase the distance from the vehicle ahead.,b:Keep the same distance as normal.,c:Follow more closely than usual.
note: You need extra distance to stop on slippery pavement; maintain a longer following distance.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.,c:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces your ability to avoid a collision if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,b:Assert your right-of-way over the pedestrians.,c:Proceed because vehicles have priority.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, including when turning on a steady green light.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:A construction zone ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.
note: Dashed yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic lanes and indicate passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Won't have any effect on your driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Will nearly double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly increase crash risk; each 0.02 percent increase raises the chance of a fatal crash dramatically.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.,b:Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,c:Increase the volume of your radio.
note: If fatigue affects your driving, safely pull over and take a short nap or rest to refresh before continuing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to stop unless necessary for safety.

question: How should you drive in work zones?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Increase your speed to get through quickly.
note: Slow down, obey posted speed limits, and be prepared to stop in work zones. Be alert for workers and changing road conditions.

question: At night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive?
options: a:Turn on high beams to see further ahead.,b:Keep your instrument lights bright to be visible to others.,c:Slow so you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the illuminated area of your headlights.

question: When exiting an interstate, when should you slow down?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane; once in the deceleration lane, reduce speed to the exit ramp advisory speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling you should:
options: a:Merge carefully into the gap.,b:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.
note: Accelerate to the speed of traffic, signal, and merge smoothly into an appropriate gap. Do not assume other drivers will automatically yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Delaware law does not grant right-of-way; what does it specify instead?
options: a:Who must yield the right-of-way.,b:Nothing about the right-of-way.,c:That right-of-way does not exist.
note: Delaware statutes describe who must yield, not who has an absolute right-of-way.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the wheels toward the side of the road (toward the curb).,c:Keep the wheels straight.
note: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or road edge so the vehicle will stop against the curb if it rolls.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beams in fog.,b:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,c:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.
note: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check mirrors every 2–5 seconds. Do not use high beams in fog; use low beams instead.

question: If you've had several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is to:
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait several hours.,c:Drink several cups of coffee.
note: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body; other measures like coffee or showers don't speed sobriety. About one hour per drink.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing.,b:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: Do not pass in intersections or where your view is blocked by curves or hills. Only pass where signage and pavement markings allow and it is safe to do so.

question: What does a single broken white centerline mean on the roadway?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,c:You may cross the line to change lanes.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

question: Stopping distance and the severity of crashes:
options: a:Increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,c:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.
note: Stopping distances and crash severity grow with higher speeds; speed significantly affects the outcome of collisions.

question: Collisions are more likely when how many vehicles are traveling relative to each other?
options: a:One lane travels faster but all others match each other.,b:All vehicles travel at about the same speed.,c:One vehicle is traveling much faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Crashes are more likely when a vehicle is traveling noticeably faster or slower than surrounding traffic.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the safest response?
options: a:Turn your lights on and off.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Glance toward the right edge of the road.
note: Look toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights and to stay safely on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed with caution, checking for cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct method to make a right turn?
options: a:Approach the corner in the lane nearest the right curb,b:Signal,c:Use turn indicator
note: Approach the intersection from the right lane, signal, slow down, and stay as close as practicable to the right curb or edge when making a right turn.

question: If your wheels run off the edge of the pavement, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.,b:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: If you leave the roadway, keep the steering wheel steady, ease off the gas, and slow down gradually before checking traffic and re-entering the road safely.

question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,b:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.,c:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
note: Driving too fast for conditions or above speed limits is a common factor in crashes. Drive within legal limits and adjust speed for conditions.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as which of the following?
options: a:Neither of the above.,b:A stimulant.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows nerve impulses and bodily functions, impairing driving ability.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Only watch for multiple trains.,b:Only watch for vehicles that must stop.,c:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and watch for multiple trains.
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution. Be aware of vehicles (e.g., school buses, hazardous material trucks) that are required to stop and of the possibility of more than one train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed:
options: a:Helps you maneuver around obstacles safely.,b:Saves time in most trips.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed is a major factor in crashes and increases both stopping distance and crash severity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the left lane and traffic is passing you on the right, what should you do if the driver behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let the other vehicles pass.,b:Stay in your lane so you don't impede the flow of traffic.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.
note: Use the left lane for passing or faster traffic. If you are driving slower than surrounding traffic, move to the right lane when it is safe.

question: You may legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate:
options: a:When the warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Never.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Wait until the gate is fully raised and it is safe to proceed.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is accurate?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair driving.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs, as well as illegal drugs, can impair driving and make it illegal to drive while impaired.

question: How can you avoid glare from the headlights of an approaching car at night?
options: a:Stay focused on the centerline on the road.,b:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: Avoid staring at oncoming headlights; glance toward the right edge of the road briefly and use peripheral vision to monitor the oncoming vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, what should you yield to?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,c:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.
note: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what is the proper action?
options: a:Merge across two lanes at once.,b:Always stop before entering the highway.,c:Select a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed and merge when a safe gap appears; do not stop unless necessary.

question: When should you use high beam headlights at night?
options: a:Whenever driving at night as often as possible.,b:When following other vehicles closely.,c:Only when there are no oncoming vehicles and you are not closely following another vehicle.
note: Use high beams only when you are not following another vehicle closely and there are no oncoming cars to avoid blinding others.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination only.,b:Alertness and concentration only.,c:All of the above (alertness
note: Alcohol and many drugs impair alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination, reducing driving ability.

question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, what should you first do?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Before stopping, check mirrors and surrounding traffic so you can slow smoothly and safely.

question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:
options: a:To warn others of the bad weather.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: When you must use windshield wipers due to weather, also turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds indicate:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:General warning signs.,c:Construction and maintenance warning signs.
note: The color orange is used specifically for signs related to construction and maintenance activity ahead.

question: Which statement about alcohol's effects on driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgement,b:If you are under the legal BAC limit,c:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking
note: Alcohol impairs judgment — a critical skill for safe driving. Even amounts below the legal limit can affect your driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b:Change lanes without signaling.,c:If you miss your exit
note: You should always signal when changing lanes. On interstates, stay in the right lane if you are moving slower than the flow of traffic; do not back up or make U-turns.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You do not need to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is ending and you should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,c:You should speed up to complete your turn.
note: A yellow arrow warns that the green protected turn is ending; be prepared to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: If your view to the side at an intersection is blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,b:Stop,c:Slow down and look both ways.
note: If cross traffic is obscured, stop and slowly inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Share the lane with the motorcycle because it is small.,c:Blow your horn to make the rider move onto the shoulder.
note: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Do not crowd the cyclist or share the same lane space with them.

question: How might a large truck turning right across two lanes behave?
options: a:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Long vehicles often need to swing wide when turning because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

question: Traffic control devices used in construction and maintenance work areas are what color?
options: a:Red.,b:Yellow.,c:Orange.
note: Work zone signs, cones, and barriers are orange to alert drivers to temporary road work conditions.

question: When driving next to a single broken white line on a highway, you:
options: a:Cannot cross the line to pass.,b:May cross the line to pass or change lanes when it is safe.,c:May cross only if you are in the left lane.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

question: Before entering an intersection, what scanning sequence should you use?
options: a:Look only to the right.,b:Look left,c:Look only to the left.
note: Look left, right, then left again before entering an intersection because vehicles from the left will be closer.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Drivers may turn after a complete stop only.,b:Drivers must stop before turning.,c:Traffic may turn in the indicated direction and has the right-of-way.
note: A green arrow gives directional right-of-way to traffic turning in the arrow's direction, though caution is still required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only if you increase your speed before the turn.,b:If traffic on the street you are turning onto moves to the left.,c:Only if traffic on the street moves to the right.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street that carries traffic to the left, unless signs prohibit the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, what should you do first?
options: a:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.,b:Check behind you,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check rear and side traffic, then gauge the forward gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:Speed does not affect driving safety.
note: Driving significantly slower than traffic can create hazards; it is safest to travel with the flow within legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,b:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop before entering.,c:Continue through the intersection
note: If you are in the intersection, clear it and then pull to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Even a single drink can impair driving ability. It is not advisable to drive after consuming any amount of alcohol.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around them.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c:Continue ahead; you have the right-of-way.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and wait until the crossing is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how should you execute the pass?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
note: Execute passes efficiently to minimize time spent in the opposing lane and return when safe to do so.

question: When taking any medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Have someone follow you home.,c:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about how it may affect driving.
note: Prescription and OTC medications can impair driving; confirm their effects with a healthcare professional.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Coordination only.,b:Alertness only.,c:Both alertness and coordination.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair multiple driving skills including alertness, coordination, and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must you obey when they are directing traffic at a construction site?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Drivers must obey instructions from flaggers and signal persons; they protect both workers and motorists.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway in bad weather, you should:
options: a:Tailgate so the truck driver can see you.,b:Keep no more than one car length behind the truck.,c:Follow farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
note: Maintain a greater following distance behind large trucks so you have enough time to stop and so the truck driver can see you if you are not directly visible in the mirrors.

question: When driving in fog, what is the correct action?
options: a:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait until conditions improve.

question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard flashers and keep driving.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.,c:Reduce speed
note: With heavy smoke ahead, slow down, move as far right as possible, and stop off the road before deciding whether it's safe to continue.

question: As your travel speed increases, you should:
options: a:Change lanes frequently to find a faster lane.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle to allow time to react.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: Stopping distance grows with speed. At higher speeds you must look farther ahead so you have enough time and distance to respond safely to hazards.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what is the best action?
options: a:Speed up to increase distance from the tailgater.,b:Apply your brakes to slow down suddenly and then resume speed.,c:Slow down gradually to encourage them to pass.
note: If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce speed to encourage the tailgater to pass; avoid sudden maneuvers.

question: What is true about pedestrians at a crosswalk?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. Where signals are not present, vehicles must stop for pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Slow down and drive around the gates.,b:Drive around the crossing gates if you cannot see a train.,c:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warning devices indicate a train is approaching. It is illegal and dangerous to drive around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever allowed to drive off the roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.,c:No — under no circumstances.
note: You may not drive off the paved or main-traveled portion of the roadway to pass another vehicle.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, you should do all of the following EXCEPT:
options: a:Let go of the steering wheel.,b:Press your head firmly against the head restraint.,c:Apply your brakes.
note: If struck from behind, press against the back of the seat and head restraint to reduce whiplash and be ready to brake. Do not let go of the steering wheel.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:
options: a:Hazards.,b:Dangerous.,c:Vehicles.
note: Bicycles are legally treated as vehicles on roadways; bicyclists and motorists must follow the same rules of the road.

question: A curb painted red indicates:
options: a:A loading zone.,b:An area reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park in that area.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem (triangle) on the rear of a vehicle indicate?
options: a:The vehicle makes sudden stops.,b:The vehicle is being drawn by an animal.,c:The vehicle is traveling at 25 mph or slower.
note: A triangular slow-moving vehicle emblem warns other drivers the vehicle travels at 25 mph or less.

question: Which surface tends to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:An intersection.,b:A tunnel.,c:A bridge.
note: Bridges and overpasses can freeze before nearby roadways because their surfaces cool from both above and below.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful?
options: a:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,c:Both of the above.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no passing zones and at locations such as railroad crossings, hills, curves, and intersections where visibility is limited.

question: Which road area is most likely to become icy in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A residential road.,b:A hilly,c:A road in a shaded area.
note: Shaded parts of the roadway freeze before others and tend to stay icy longer on cold days.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of freeway traffic.,c:At the posted speed limit regardless of traffic speed.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of the traffic flow so you can merge safely without disrupting other vehicles.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:Near blind pedestrians.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:If you might hit another vehicle.
note: Avoid sounding your horn near blind pedestrians as it may be dangerous; yield and proceed only when safe.

question: When driving in fog, which lights are best to use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams will reflect back and reduce visibility further.

question: What is the only thing that will reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and remove alcohol's effects from your body?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat,b:Time,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only the passage of time eliminates alcohol from the body; caffeine or food do not sober you up or lower BAC.

question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line on a multilane road mean?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only drivers adjacent to the dashed line may cross to pass; drivers next to the solid line may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but the intersection is blocked with traffic, you should:
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b:Wait and not enter the intersection until you can clear it completely.,c:Enter and wait within the intersection for traffic to clear.
note: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely across before the light changes; blocking an intersection is illegal.

question: What does a red right-pointing arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.,b:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
note: A red arrow means stop and remain stopped; you may not turn until a green light or arrow appears.

question: What is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,c:Be constantly alert.
note: Driving on interstates requires being constantly alert and capable of safely operating at higher speeds.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way?
options: a:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,b:Only if the pedestrian has a Walk signal.,c:Any pedestrian crossing any street or in any crosswalk.
note: Yield to pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks and generally to anyone crossing the street to avoid striking them.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,b:You should use cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a steady speed.,c:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.
note: Stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal directs you to do so. Always use caution near tracks.

question: Which practice best helps you avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Keep your eyes focused only ahead of your car.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Always be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
note: Constantly scanning front, sides, and rear helps you detect hazards early and take appropriate action to avoid them.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean?
options: a:The lane to the right may pass.,b:No passing is allowed from either direction.,c:Both lanes may pass when safe.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite directions of traffic and prohibit passing from both sides.

question: Yellow lines on the road separate:
options: a:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
note: Yellow centerlines divide opposing traffic; solid and broken markings convey passing rules.
